summary: Facepalm: Facepalm scan for 2026-11-03 (window Oct. 28–Nov. 3). The search quota ran out partway through, so only one candidate was found. Westchester County, N.Y.: on Election Day, voting machines across the county rejected paper ballots. NBC New York and ABC7 New York both covered it, and so did PBS NewsHour's live updates. The Board of Elections attributed it to an issue involving paper ballots and apologized. Its exact cause was still unresolved at scan time: the board first blamed paper thickness, then removed that word from its statement. Several other leads were set aside for lack of accepted sources, age, or exclusions. Genius: Genius scan for 2026-11-03 (window Oct. 28 – Nov. 3). I'm submitting one candidate: the Milwaukee Brewers winning the first World Series title in franchise history on Oct. 28 in St. Petersburg, Fla. Two accepted publishers cover it, WPR and Fox News, and I opened both pages and checked the quotes against them. It falls on the first day of the window. It is a sports championship, not the scientific or ingenuity story the site prefers, but it is a clearly established first. The search limit ran out early. After the code session reset, opening pages also stopped working ('url not in prior context'), so I couldn't find second sources for several promising sports leads: the Valkyries' first WNBA title, Zouhair Talbi's best-ever NYC Marathon time by an American, and Jack Alexy's world record. The ScienceDaily and Science News items I could open were all outside the US, older reposts, mouse studies or published before the window. Pair published.

candidates.headline: Milwaukee Brewers win the franchise's first World Series title, beating the Rays in Game 5
candidates.reason: passed every check

candidates.headline: Westchester County, N.Y., voting machines reject paper ballots countywide on Election Day
candidates.reason: passed every check

candidates.headline: FBI New Haven office post tells voters Election Day is Wednesday
candidates.reason: In the window (Nov. 3), but the only coverage found was the New Haven Independent, IBTimes, Lead Stories, Raw Story (banned), Substack and X, none of which is accepted. Searches of CT Insider and WTNH found nothing.

candidates.headline: Bladen County, N.C., poll worker prints wrong ballots
candidates.reason: In the window (Nov. 3), but the only coverage found was Border Belt Independent, which isn't on the accepted list.

candidates.headline: Duval County, Fla., polling places hit by a broken tabulator and power outages
candidates.reason: Action News Jax reports that a broken machine and a neighborhood power outage were handled quickly with generators. That is an equipment failure and an outage, not a blunder.

candidates.headline: NFL fines Lions safety Brian Branch for an unflagged hit, read as admitting an officiating miss in the Packers game
candidates.reason: The fine was framed as an 'admission' only by non-accepted outlets (A to Z Sports, Yardbarker, EssentiallySports). No accepted source reporting an NFL admission was found.

candidates.headline: Florida Department of Education systems breached, exposing Social Security numbers
candidates.reason: The agency was the victim of a hack (a crime with victims), which the rules exclude.

candidates.headline: Snohomish County, Wash., ballot envelopes misspell 'general'
candidates.reason: Reported about 15–21 days before the scan date, outside the 7-day window.

candidates.headline: Seattle Police Department overpaid officers $13 million in a payroll error
candidates.reason: Reported about Oct. 1, outside the 7-day window.

candidates.headline: Richmond, Va., police chief apologizes for a car damaged in a wrongful tow
candidates.reason: The car owner is on the receiving end of the error, and the only source seen (12 On Your Side) isn't on the accepted list.

candidates.headline: New Jersey MVC voter-registration errors
candidates.reason: A long-running issue that began before the window and centers on noncitizen registration, which touches immigration status. Coverage seen was mostly non-accepted outlets.

candidates.headline: Golden State Valkyries beat the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in Game 7 at Chase Center, San Francisco, for the franchise's first WNBA title (Oct. 31)
candidates.reason: In the US and inside the window, but the only accepted page I opened is Fox News/OutKick (Oct. 31). The search limit ran out before I could find a second accepted publisher. Worth retrying.

candidates.headline: Zouhair Talbi runs the fastest NYC Marathon ever by an American man (2:06:43, sixth place, Nov. 1)
candidates.reason: Only one accepted source opened (ABC7 New York, Nov. 2). The other confirmation is New York Road Runners' own release, and nyrr.org is not an accepted publisher or official source. Worth retrying.

candidates.headline: NYC Marathon becomes the first marathon with more than 60,000 finishers (61,146, Nov. 1)
candidates.reason: The only coverage seen was NYRR's own release, NBC Sports (via Yahoo), Marathon Handbook and Running USA, none of which is accepted. It is also a turnout figure rather than an achievement.

candidates.headline: Jack Alexy sets short-course 100m freestyle world record (44.64) at U.S. trials in Westmont, Ill. (Oct. 30)
candidates.reason: Still only one accepted source (Fox News/OutKick, Oct. 31). Yahoo's copy is a republication of the Fox story, and the other coverage (SwimSwam, Swimming World, The Sports Examiner) is not accepted.

candidates.headline: Brewers reliever Aaron Ashby sets MLB record for consecutive scoreless innings by a reliever in one postseason
candidates.reason: Too old. The record came in World Series Game 4 on Tuesday, Oct. 27, one day before the window. The only coverage seen was Yahoo Sports, which is not accepted.

candidates.headline: IceCube detects neutrinos with 10 billion times the energy of solar neutrinos (ScienceDaily, Nov. 2)
candidates.reason: The detector is at the South Pole, not in the US. ScienceDaily's page is a UC San Diego feature that cites a 1998 PRL paper, so I couldn't identify a new result inside the window.

candidates.headline: Electronic implant converts excess blood sugar and causes weight loss in diabetic mice (Science)
candidates.reason: Not in the US (ETH Zurich). It is also a mouse study.

candidates.headline: Electrically driven single-molecule 'Archimedes screw' motor (Nature)
candidates.reason: Not in the US. The source is the University of Augsburg, and the authors are from European and Israeli institutions.

candidates.headline: UVA ultrasound-delivered treatment extends survival in glioblastoma animal models
candidates.reason: An animal study with 'could' framing. The only accepted source is a ScienceDaily repost, and the paper date was not confirmed inside the window.

candidates.headline: Gladstone Institutes finds a bacterial retron defense that works in reverse (Molecular Cell)
candidates.reason: A basic mechanism finding rather than a distinct achievement. The only accepted source is a ScienceDaily repost, and the publication date was not confirmed inside the window.

candidates.headline: Johns Hopkins finds vitamin A derivative patterns foveal cones (PNAS)
candidates.reason: Too old. The paper is in PNAS vol. 123, issue 7, an earlier 2026 issue, and ScienceDaily's Oct. 31 page is a repost. It was already set aside on Nov. 2.

candidates.headline: Alloys stay tough at 20 kelvin through competing mechanisms (Nature)
candidates.reason: Too old. ScienceDaily says the paper was published Oct. 14, 2026, before the window.

candidates.headline: Vera C. Rubin Observatory reveals its first dwarf planet candidate (2026 ED138)
candidates.reason: The observatory is in Chile, not the US. It was announced Oct. 27, before the window, and the coverage seen (Fox News, Astronomy) included only one accepted page, which I did not open.

candidates.headline: DNA from Thomas Jefferson's hair strengthens evidence he fathered Sally Hemings' children
candidates.reason: Too old. Fox News published it Sept. 24, 2026.
